note: Labeled scope statements from the production backup of 2026-10-01 (holdout projects excluded), written and frozen before the WS5 attribution classifier. carry: exclude = the statement assigns physical scope (work or equipment) to a party other than the electrical contractor; include = it assigns physical scope to the electrical contractor (an electrical sheet's contractor or an imperative electrical note); neutral = administrative, coordination, code reference, product standard without a party on an electrical sheet, or no obligation. In an owner exhibit or Division 01 text the contractor or successful bidder is the prime (gc). No dollar figures.

statements.text: The work includes the removal of walls, mechanical systems, plumbing fixtures, and electrical elements.
It is the contractor's responsibility to patch and repair as required to match existing building's finishes.
All patch and repair work done outside the limit of the new construction shall be included as part of the scope of work.

The general contractor shall furnish, install, and maintain suitable barriers (fire-rated where required) in compliance with the infection control risk assessment as required to prevent public entry into all work areas.
The general contractor shall provide electrical, data, and plumbing connections from infrastructure to pre-manufactured furniture systems.
The general contractor is responsible for contacting and coordinating with Honeywell prior to demolition to disarm the existing system.
Time of work will be after business hours (6:00 am - 3:30 pm) Monday through Friday.
Access controls and all Fire detection systems for the building are provided by Honeywell.
Any additional or new card readers will need to be integrated with the Honeywell access controls system.

Telemetry antennas, Centrak devices, and wireless access point exact locations must be noted on a marked-up floor plan delivered to the engineering representative prior to any demolition. Removal, storage, and re-installation of these devices shall be the responsibility of the SUCCESSFUL BIDDER.
SUCCESSFUL BIDDER must be able to demonstrate experience working in an operational hospital.
General contractors shall possess a valid B - General Building license, in accordance with NRS, Chapter 624.
All subcontractors shall possess the appropriate valid specialty license(s), in accordance with NRS, Chapter 624.
Nevada Revised Statutes (NRS), Chapter 338 - Public Works
Contractor is responsible for daily clean up and removal of refuse from areas of work.
Contractor will furnish and install proper floor and wall protection for existing finishes.
Contractor will provide a dumpster for projects determined to generate more than 3 yards of refuse.
Contractor is responsible to set up full containment area(s), and negative air filtration systems for the scope of work.
Contractor will provide a copy of their current Safety Manual to UMC's Safety Department.
Contractor will secure all HVAC ducting when performance of work creates dust or smoke particulates as necessary to prevent contamination of existing duct systems.
Contractor will follow and be compliant with any Interim Life Safety Management plans (ILSM) when deemed necessary.
Contractor is responsible for sealing of all penetrations disturbed or created in performance of contract work.
Obtain any required permits and pay all associated fees.
Secure/cover fire alarm smoke detectors in areas of construction to avoid false alarms.
All work to take place during hours of (6:00am - 3:30pm) Monday - Friday.
Responsible for the replacement, as well as patching or repair, of any of the building materials or adjacent surfaces damaged while performing scope of work.
Standard toilet tissue, paper towel, soap, hand sanitizer dispensers, sharps container, glove box holders and PDI wipe holders shall be furnished by Owner and installed by Contractor.
All long lead materials shall be ordered for the project no later than two (2) weeks after issuance of an associated Purchase Order.
All utility disruptions must be scheduled with UMC's Engineering Department at least 48 hours in advance.
Cylindrical locksets: Schlage or equal ND series prepped for large format interchangeable core, Rhodes lever 626 finish
Exit Devices: Von Duprin 99 Series or equal - rim panics on single doors, concealed vertical rods panics less bottom rod on pairs (no surface rods).
Low Energy Auto Operators: LCN Senior Swing operators. Pair - 9550 Series. Single - 9530/9540 series. Power Supply - Von Duprin PS 914 or equal
Door and Frame Paint Spec / Sherwin-Williams - Substitutes for paint brand and sheen are not acceptable.
UMC Paint Standards for walls/ceilings Dunn Edwards Versasatin

The general contractor and subcontractors are responsible for referencing the permit set - construction documents; architectural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing to include scope of work, specifications, general notes, keyed notes, sheet indexes, and legend.

General Contractor shall coordinate and schedule with the facility all demolition and construction not less than 72 hours prior to work in any areas that will maintain operations and patient treatment.
Major utility disruptions shall be scheduled 48 hours in advance and will need to be performed in the after business hours (off hours) for the occupants.

CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL OPENINGS REQUIRED IN WALLS. ALL OPENINGS SHALL BE REPAIRED TO MATCH EXISTING BY A QUALIFIED CONTRACTOR AT THE EXPENSE OF THIS CONTRACTOR. ALL CONDUITS THROUGH WALLS SHALL BE GROUTED OR SEALED INTO OPENINGS.

ALL RECEPTACLES INSTALLED IN PATIENT CARE AREAS SHALL BE HOSPITAL GRADE DEVICES WITH GREEN DOT. ALL RECEPTACLES IN OFFICES, CORRIDORS SHALL BE TAMPER RESISTANT PER NEC ARTICLES 517 AND 406.12.

THE ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE OUTLETS AND RACEWAYS FOR COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS AS INDICATED HEREIN.
CONNECT ALL EQUIPMENT, SYSTEMS, AND ASSEMBLIES PROVIDED BY OTHERS INCLUDING CONTROLS, SAFETY DEVICES AND INTERCONNECTIONS.

EXISTING FIRE ALARM SYSTEM - DESIGN/BUILD REVISIONS: AUGMENT/EXPAND FIRE ALARM CONTROL PANEL AND ANNUNCIATOR TO ACCOMMODATE ADDED DEVICES AND CIRCUITING AS REQUIRED TO ACCOMMODATE NEW WORK.
EMT WITH STEEL INSULATED THROAT SET SCREW FITTINGS MAY BE USED IN DRY, PROTECTED INTERIOR LOCATIONS.
ALL WIRING ABOVE CEILING SHALL BE IN RIGID CONDUIT. NO EXPOSED ELEMENTS SHALL BE ALLOWED. MC CABLE SHALL NOT BE ALLOWED.
MAINTAIN IN CONSTANT OPERATION DURING THIS PROJECT. (ENERGY COSTS BY OTHERS).

NEW LOCATION FOR RELOCATED THEATRICAL DIMMING CONTROLS. PROVIDE CONDUCTORS, CONTROL WIRING, ETC. AS REQUIRED TO EXTEND EXISTING CONTROLS TO NEW DEVICE LOCATION. COORDINATE WITH ARCHITECT/OWNER'S REPRESENTATIVE FOR FINAL RELOCATED LOCATION PRIOR TO ROUGH-IN.

GFI MARKED ON THE PLAN INDICATES THAT THE CIRCUIT SHALL BE GFI PROTECTED. E.C. SHALL PROVIDE A GFCI BREAKER IN THE PANEL FOR THE INDICATED CIRCUIT IF EITHER THE RECEPTACLE IS NOT AVAILABLE OR NOT READILY ACCESSIBLE.

ALL WORK SHALL BE PERFORMED BY A LICENSED ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR IN A FIRST CLASS WORKMANLIKE MANNER. THE COMPLETED SYSTEM SHALL BE FULLY OPERATIVE AND ACCEPTED BY ENGINEER/ARCHITECT.
ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR SHALL GUARANTEE ALL MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP FREE FROM DEFECTS FOR A PERIOD OF NOT LESS THAN ONE YEAR FROM DATE THAT CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY IS ISSUED.

Contractor shall be responsible for the transport, storage, and safeguarding of all removed Bus Shelter units at a secure facility approved by the RTC.
Contractor shall procure and install four (4) metal shrouds per shelter to cover security tamper proof screws at each dedicated bus stop location.
Contractor shall procure and install safety steel bollards behind and/or both sides of shelter.
At each proposed bus stop shelter pad location, Contractor shall excavate, haul away and dispose of soils, landscaping, and/or vegetation.
For materials sampling and testing, RTC shall provide third party special inspections.
The Contractor shall provide a baseline schedule from project initiation to final acceptance with commencement and completion dates, for review no later than 10 calendar days after Notice of Award.
Contractor shall provide color samples for RTC approval.
Lock keys shall be returned to RTC.
Contractor shall coordinate in advance with the RTC field representative all required materials testing and third-party special inspections.
Jurisdictionally required traffic control permits shall be the sole responsibility of the Contractor.
Security hardware shall be shipped directly to RTC.

Contractor shall reference RTC provided jurisdictional approved RTC Standalone Light Pole plan sheet and provide separate bid line-item cost for removal, temporary storage, and reinstallation upon completion of new bus shelter pad construction.
Contractor shall provide RTC all required submittals, including Buy America certifications/certificates.

The Contractor shall perform all Work and provide all labor, equipment, materials, transportation, and supervision necessary to complete the interior renovation of the existing Day Room at Fire Station 95.
The Contractor shall be responsible for protecting existing conditions and all areas affected by performance of the Work.
The Contractor shall be responsible for all cleanup associated with the Project.
The Contractor shall be responsible for submitting all required permit applications and supporting documentation necessary to obtain permits associated with the Work.
Work shall be performed Monday - Friday between the hours of 7:30am - 5:30pm.
Contractor shall submit weekly certified payroll reports in accordance with prevailing wage requirements.
The Contractor shall be required to submit criminal background check forms for approval for all workers scheduled to perform construction activities within or around the facility.
Upon completion of the Work, the Contractor shall remove all remaining trash, debris, and construction waste and leave the affected areas in a clean condition.
Costs of any temporary lighting shall be included in the amount bid for Traffic Control.
Contractor shall be responsible to install an 8-inch solid white edge line to establish the edge of travel way before the barriers are installed.
Contractor shall prepare pedestrian detour plans, depicting Contractor's intended temporary walkways, for the Engineer's approval prior to removal of existing sidewalk or existing asphalt sidewalk.
Roadway lighting shall be maintained at all times.
All pipe and conduit with individual nominal diameters 4-inches or less shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional payment will be made.
Contractor shall stage the work at each intersection to accommodate turning vehicles, including trucks, at all times.
A work plan shall be submitted showing areas of work, durations and days for each work area proposed that will need to be coordinated with the authority based on the current show schedule.
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL WORK, MATERIALS, AND EQUIPMENT UNTIL FINAL ACCEPTANCE BY THE OWNER.
This bid item excludes all electrical work as shown in the Electrical Drawings to be done by others under a separate contract.
Protect Owner-furnished items from damage during storage and handling, including damage from exposure to the elements.
